name: Disodium pyrophosphate
description: Disodium pyrophosphate ( CAS 7758-16-9 ), also known as SAPP and sodium acid pyrophosphate, is an inorganic phosphate salt used across food manufacturing and water treatment as a buffering, leavening, and sequestering agent. Approved as E450a in the EU, it controls pH, binds metal ions, and stabilizes formulations where precise acidity management is critical. In baked goods, SAPP acts as a leavening acid in baking powder and self-rising flour. It reacts with sodium bicarbonate to generate controlled CO₂ release during baking. Potato processors rely on it to inhibit after-cooking darkening by chelating iron and other trace metals that trigger enzymatic discoloration. In seafood and meat processing, it functions as a moisture stabilizer and texture modifier, reducing drip loss in frozen products. Water treatment operations use it to sequester hardness ions and control scale formation. Disodium pyrophosphate is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granules, with granule grades available for improved flowability in dry blending operations. Standard market grades include food-grade material. This material conforms to FCC and E450a specifications, as well as technical-grade material for industrial applications. Buyers should confirm the slow-acting or fast-acting leavening profile when sourcing. The reaction rate varies by grade, making it essential to select the correct version for specific baking applications.
